thread:
alex: I built a quick prototype of an admission/routing gateway that mediates requests across VRAM, host RAM, NVMe and remote staging. Wanted to float the design and API before formalizing an RFC.

marie: Is this meant to sit inside the runner, or as a standalone control plane service?

alex: My plan: start in-process as a pluggable module behind a feature flag, then split into a service if we need multi-process sharing. It exposes a tiny RPC-ish surface even when in-process to keep the integration stable.

sam: Give a sketch of the lifecycle for a single request. Concerned about extra RTTs.

alex: Flow: request -> Gateway.GetToken(tenant, model, meta) -> returns {token, route, weight, ttl} -> caller proceeds to allocate/use route -> caller calls Gateway.ReleaseToken(token, result). Optionally NotifyPrefetch can be fire-and-forget. Single fast synchronous call for admission.

vijay: How do you model budgets? Per-device? per-tenant? per-model?

alex: Hierarchical: global per-tenant hard cap, per-device soft/hard caps, and optional per-model prioritization. We score tokens by type so prefetches count less than blocking generation work.

lina: Token taxonomy?

alex: Three canonical types: `blocking` (generation), `prefetch` (speculative KV fetch), `evict-hint` (caller suggests freeing pages). Each gets a `weight` multiplier in policy so budgets are comparable.

sam: Fallbacks: if NVMe is saturated do we route to remote? fall back to host? We need predictable behavior to avoid tail cliffs.

alex: Gateway ranks fallback routes and exposes the chosen route along with expected p95/p99 latencies and a cost score. Caller chooses one of two modes: `strict` (fail on non-local) and `adaptive` (accept fallback). Default is `adaptive` for hosted tenants.

vijay: Closed-loop control is critical. If gateway keeps sending work to remote and remote degrades, we need to reduce admission automatically.

alex: Agreed. Gateway ingests telemetry: per-device qlen, device-p95, remote queue depth. A simple PID-ish limiter reduces route weight when latency exceeds margin. We smooth using exponential windows and enforce hysteresis to avoid oscillation.

lina: How frequent are metrics? Too frequent leads to thrash.

alex: Metrics aggregated at 1s windows, weight adjustments every 10s with smoothing factor. Operators can tune via config.

marie: Persisting quotas and auditability? Token loss on restart?


alex: Quotas live in control-plane DB; gateway caches them with TTL and checkpoints deltas. Tokens include TTL for orphan reclaim. We'll emit `token_leak_count` and `token_reclaim_events` so ops can detect issues.

sam: Integration with existing EvictHint API? We already have runners calling evict hints when memory pressure rises.


alex: EvictHint becomes soft input to the gateway's cost model, but we don't convert an EvictHint into a forced eviction token. Instead, if device usage high, gateway will prefer routes that offload and may issue `evict-hint` tokens to encourage background offload work.

vijay: Security: tokens must be tenant-scoped and auditable. Also protect against token spoofing.


alex: Tokens are opaque UUIDs signed with gateway key and validated on release. All token ops logged with tenant context.

lina: Edge cases: long-running sessions that hold tokens. How to reclaim?


alex: Tokens have TTL and a soft-heartbeat path. If heartbeat misses and TTL expires, gateway marks token stale and reclaims. We'll provide `AsyncReclaim(token)` for operators and emit tracing spans for token lifecycle.

marie: API contract? Keep minimal surface.


alex: Initial minimal RPCs: `GetToken(tenant, model, req_meta) -> {token, route, weight, ttl}`, `ReleaseToken(token, outcome)`, `NotifyPrefetch(tenant, hint)` (fire-and-forget), `ReclaimStaleTokens()` admin endpoint.

sam: Testing plan?


alex: Unit tests for policy math, integration loadbench that simulates NVMe stalls + skewed tenant traffic, and a canary rollout on host pool with a small quota. We'll also add a nightly `mem-gateway-smoke` job.

infra-bot: deploy/ci: added mem-gateway-smoke job to nightly (CI-3987).

vijay: Observability: we need per-tenant admission metrics, per-route latency estimates, and leak counters. Also traces that correlate request -> token lifecycle -> device ioctl timings.

alex: Agreed: emit `tokens_granted`, `tokens_rejected`, `token_wait_time`, `route_choice` tags, plus trace spans for `GetToken` and `ReleaseToken`.

lina: Migration: how do we flip runners to use this without regressing tail?


alex: Feature-flagged rollout: metrics-only mode first (gateway suggests routes but runners ignore), then `opt-in` per-runner, then global. We'll monitor tail and error rates per tenant.

marie: Please include a small YAML example of a per-tenant policy in the RFC. Also include failure semantics: what caller must do if `GetToken` returns `reject` vs `fallback`.

alex: Will do. Example policy snippet I'll add to RFC draft. Planning to write RFC tomorrow with API, policy knobs, control loop tuning, and migration plan.

sam: One more thought: allow callers to express urgency priority so we can preempt prefetch tokens if needed.

alex: Good idea — tokens accept `priority` and prefetch tokens are the first to be bumped. I'll add preemption rules to the design doc.

marie: :thumbsup: Looking forward to the RFC. Make sure the in-process vs svc split is clearly documented.


alex: Thanks all. Draft incoming.
